sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Lakewood, WA?
sections.html:
A Lakewood owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept an as-is cash offer, and the right choice depends on the house and on how it is being used. A vacant, well-kept house suits a listing. A house with tenants, deferred repairs or an estate attached tends to move faster in a direct sale.

Renting is unusually common in Lakewood. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 47.5 percent for 2020 to 2024, the median gross rent at $1,525 and the median value of owner-occupied homes at $461,200. The city also has a registration and inspection program for rentals, covered below, which shapes how a rented house sells.

sections.h2: How did Lakewood become a city, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Lakewood was incorporated on February 28, 1996, the same day as Edgewood, after voters had turned down incorporation in 1971, 1990 and 1994. It became the second largest city in Pierce County at once. The city has 17.06 square miles of land and many lakes, so a lot near water is a normal part of the market.

  • American Lake: the largest, at 1,091 acres and an average depth of 53 feet.
  • Lake Steilacoom, Gravelly Lake, Lake Louise and Waughop Lake: the other named lakes, with Waughop Lake inside Fort Steilacoom Park.
  • Chambers Creek: the largest creek, flowing from Lake Steilacoom toward Chambers Bay.

State Route 512 ends at its western terminus where it meets Interstate 5 in Lakewood. Pierce Transit is headquartered in the city, and the Lakewood Sounder station, which opened in 2012 as the southern end of the S Line, runs commuter trains north through Tacoma to Seattle. Census data put the mean commute at 29.3 minutes.

sections.h2: What drives Lakewood's economy and local services?
sections.html:
Joint Base Lewis-McChord, with about 55,000 employees, is the anchor of the regional economy. Lakewood had 30,662 full-time jobs in 2023, with more than 9,000 of them in health care. St. Clare Hospital was the largest employer at 598 employees, and the city recorded $1.65 billion in taxable retail sales in 2022. The Census Bureau counts 6,594 veterans among residents.

Public services are split among several providers, which matters when you fill in disclosure forms or hand over utility accounts:

  • The Clover Park School District runs the public schools for most of the city, and parts of Lakewood sit in the Steilacoom Historical and Tacoma districts.
  • Electricity comes from Lakeview Light and Power on the east side, Tacoma Power on the north side and Puget Sound Energy on the west side, which is also the only natural gas provider.
  • The Lakewood Water District supplies tap water to 17,680 connections.
  • Pierce County Public Works and Utilities maintains sanitary sewer, and the city manages stormwater.
  • The Lakewood Police Department began independent operations on November 1, 2004, and West Pierce Fire and Rescue covers the city.

sections.h2: How does Lakewood's Rental Housing Safety Program affect a sale?
sections.html:
The city's Rental Housing Safety Program requires owners of rental property to register every year, and registered properties are inspected once every five years. An initial inspection may be done by a city inspector or by a qualified private inspector, and every re-inspection is done by the city. Inspectors look at structural integrity, weather exposure, plumbing and sanitation, heat and water, ventilation, electrical wiring, exits, and smoke and carbon monoxide detectors.

An owner who fails to register can face penalties under the city's fee schedule and the Lakewood Municipal Code, and a rental business license can be revoked. A buyer of a rented house will ask for registration and inspection records, so gather them before you list. Exemptions under LMC 5.60.025 include:

  • Units occupied by the owner, or by the owner's parent or child.
  • Mobile and manufactured homes, shelters and transitional housing.
  • Condominiums and townhouses in multi-unit structures under multiple ownership, unless one owner holds them.
  • Units built in the past 10 years with a certificate of occupancy and no code violations.

Renting rooms in a home you live in does not require registration, but moving out and renting the whole house does. Contact the program at 253-512-2261 or rentals@cityoflakewood.us.

sections.h2: What are Lakewood's short-term rental rules?
sections.html: Short-term rentals of under 30 days are allowed in most zones. The city excludes Commercial 1 to 3, the Industrial Business Park, Industrial 1 and 2, Public and Semi-Public Institutional and Open Space Recreation 1 and 2. A short-term rental must register with the Rental Housing Safety Program, hold a business license, renew annually and be inspected every five years, with a free first inspection. The city handles the permit as a Type II administrative decision. Check your zoning before you promise a buyer short-term rental income.

sections.h2: When are Pierce County property taxes due for a Lakewood house?
sections.html:
Tax statements go out in February. If the amount is more than $50 it may be paid in two installments, April 30 and October 31, and an amount of $50 or less is due in full on April 30. Pierce County says that if a payment envelope is postmarked before the statutory deadline, interest and penalty are waived. October 31, 2026 fell on a Saturday, and the second-half deadline has now passed.

Pay online or at the Assessor-Treasurer's Office, 2401 S. 35th St., Room 142, Tacoma, which also has a drop box. Foreclosure avoidance payments go by cashier's check to that office. For status, call the Assessor-Treasurer hotline at (253) 798-6111. Mortgage companies follow the same payment rules as the owner.

sections.h2: What does a Lakewood seller owe and disclose at closing?
sections.html:
The seller normally pays the state real estate excise tax, which the Department of Revenue says is due on the sale date, and a city local tax is added. The graduated state rate starts at 1.1 percent on the first slice of the price under RCW 82.45.060, and the thresholds change January 1, 2027. On a sale at the $461,200 median value, the first-slice rate would give about $5,073 in state tax before the local portion.

The disclosure form under RCW 64.06.020 asks about the sewer connection, roof leaks and environmental items. The buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind unless the contract provides otherwise.

faqs.q: Do I have to register my Lakewood rental before selling?
faqs.a: Registration is required each year while the house is rented, unless an exemption applies. A buyer will want the certificate and inspection history, so register and inspect first if you have not.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lakewood house with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. The tenancy continues under state law after a sale, and a buyer who keeps the tenant will check the city's rental registration. Ask a Washington attorney how your lease and notice rules apply.

faqs.q: When are Pierce County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due April 30 and the second half October 31, and amounts of $50 or less are due in full on April 30. The next first-half deadline is April 30, 2027.

faqs.q: Are short-term rentals allowed in Lakewood?
faqs.a: Yes, in most zones, with a business license, registration in the Rental Housing Safety Program and a permit. Commercial 1 to 3 and several industrial and open space zones are excluded.

faqs.q: Who pays excise tax when a Lakewood house sells?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays, according to the Department of Revenue, and the tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. If it goes unpaid, interest accrues from the sale date.
